_readme: Masked-row screen over the batch binders (M1). A row filled black on the printed page is not a row
the document prints, so it is not captured (rule 17). The text sits under the fill and pdftotext
returns it, which is why this screen renders the page rather than reading the text layer.
Thresholds for the masked-row screen. Content is data; the mechanic is pbr_mask_screen.py.
A masked row is a filled rectangle: a long contiguous near-black run repeated over several scanlines.
min_scanlines is what separates a filled row from a table rule, which is the same width and one or two
scanlines tall. Tuned against the Glascott binder (97 001 281 572.pdf, md5 007e24fb685834aa109a08eebcc9f1cd),
where it flags pages 5, 7, 9, 13 and 15 and nothing else, and against trees new.pdf (51 pages, 0 flagged).
